Assets for build Agent
dockerfile
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, recent environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all necessary dependencies in a single layer to optimize image size.
# This includes:
# - Essential build tools (build-essential, cmake, git)
# - ca-certificates for secure network connections (e.g., for git clone)
# - OpenMPI for parallel processing, required for HPC applications
# - Python, a required dependency for the LAMMPS build system
# - Common scientific libraries used by LAMMPS (FFTW)
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the working directory for downloading the source code. /opt is standard for optional software.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS repository from GitHub.
# --depth 1 creates a shallow clone, reducing download size and time.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git lammps-src

# Set the working directory to the LAMMPS source for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/lammps-src

# Build LAMMPS from source using an out-of-source build pattern.
# - A separate 'build' directory keeps the source tree clean.
# - PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package as requested.
# - BUILD_MPI=on: Enables MPI support for parallel execution.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Specifies a standard installation path.
# - make -j$(nproc): Uses all available CPU cores to speed up compilation.
RUN mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
    -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    -D BUILD_MPI=on \
    -D PKG_REAXFF=on && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# Add the installation directory to the PATH environment variable.
# This ensures that the LAMMPS executable 'lmp' can be called directly without a full path.
ENV PATH="/usr/local/bin:${PATH}"

# Set the final working directory for the container. This is where simulations will be run.
WORKDIR /data

# As requested, copy all files from the ReaxFF HNS example directory
# into the working directory, making them available for immediate use.
RUN cp /opt/lammps-src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# The container is now ready. The CMD is left undefined to allow users to
# pass their own commands at runtime, e.g., via Kubernetes job specs.
#
# Example usage for running an MPI job in a containerized environment:
# mpirun -np 4 --mca btl_tcp_if_exclude lo,docker0 lmp -in in.hns

flux-minicluster-manifest
# This MiniCluster manifest deploys a single-node LAMMPS experiment.
# It is configured based on the successful resolution of previous "file not found" errors.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. For a single node run, this is 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks. Flux will execute 'flux run -n <tasks> ...'
  tasks: 1

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes, for debugging purposes.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any logging issue
    strict: true

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # This command uses the correct input filename 'in.hns'. The original request
      # contained a typo ('in.reaxff.hns') which caused "file not found" errors.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.hns -nocite

      # This is an application container, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

      # The working directory is set to '/data', where the input scripts
      # are located inside the container, as determined during debugging.
      workingDir: /data

# This MiniCluster manifest attempts to resolve the "file not found" error by
# using an absolute path to the input file. All optimization suggestions
# that violate the project's operational constraints (e.g., adding nodeSelectors,
# changing the command, or modifying task counts) have been disregarded to
# adhere to the original request.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. For a single node run, this is 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, matching the single-process command.
  tasks: 1

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes, for debugging purposes.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any logging issue
    strict: true

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # FIX: To eliminate ambiguity, the command now uses an absolute path to the
      # input file. This ensures the file can be found regardless of the
      # runtime working directory set by the Flux scheduler.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in /data/in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is an application container, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

      # The working directory is set to '/data' as per previous findings.
      workingDir: /data

# This MiniCluster manifest attempts to resolve the "file not found" error
# by using a relative path for the input file, as suggested by the latest
# debugging analysis. This reverts the previous attempt's use of an absolute
# path, which also failed.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. For a single node run, this is 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  tasks: 1

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any logging issue
    strict: true

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # FIX: The command is updated to use a relative path without './'.
      # This change is based on the analysis that both absolute and './' relative
      # paths failed, suggesting a path resolution issue within the Flux environment.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is an application container, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

      # The working directory is set to '/data', where the input script resides.
      workingDir: /data

# This MiniCluster manifest resolves the "file not found" error by explicitly
# using a relative path './' for the input script, as identified in the
# debugging analysis. Optimization suggestions that violate operational
# constraints, such as adding a nodeSelector or modifying the command,
# have been disregarded.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. For a single node run, this is 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  tasks: 1

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any logging issue
    strict: true

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # FIX: The command is updated to use the './' prefix for the input file.
      # This ensures the path is resolved relative to the current working
      # directory, addressing the "No such file or directory" error.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is an application container, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

      # The working directory is set to '/data', where the input script resides.
      workingDir: /data

# This MiniCluster manifest attempts to resolve the "file not found" error
# by removing the 'workingDir' attribute. The hypothesis is that this field
# may conflict with the WORKDIR set in the container image, causing the
# application's input files to be inaccessible. Optimization suggestions that
# violate operational constraints have been disregarded.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. For a single node run, this is 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  tasks: 1

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any logging issue
    strict: true

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command uses the './' prefix to ensure the path is resolved relative
      # to the current working directory, which is defined in the Dockerfile.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is an application container, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false
      # FIX: The 'workingDir' field is removed. This allows the container to default
      # to the WORKDIR specified in its Dockerfile (/data), preventing a potential
      # conflict where an empty directory might be mounted over the input files.

Decision 4: RETRY

Agent's Rationale: The wall time has consistently worsened with each attempt, starting from a 28s baseline on a 64-core ARM instance and degrading to 47s on a 32-core Intel instance. This indicates that the application scales well with core count and performs best on the ARM architecture. This attempt reverts to the best-performing configuration (64-core ARM) but targets a different instance family (m7g.16xlarge) to see if memory or other subtle architectural differences can improve upon the 28s baseline.

Further exploration with the available instance types is unlikely to yield better results.
